{%- comment -%}
A curated map of this site for language models, following the /llms.txt
convention: one markdown file at a well-known location that says what the site
is, how it may be reused, and where the authoritative pages are — so that a
model or an agent fetching it lands on the real documentation instead of
reconstructing it from whatever fragments it happens to have seen.

Generated from the sidebar YAML rather than from a directory listing, so it
inherits the curated reading order of the documentation and cannot drift out of
sync with the navigation. Sidebars are themselves generated by matlab/xml2yml.m
from the .toc files, so a page added to a .toc appears here automatically.

Scope: documentation and examples in full, plus the eight section indexes of the
function reference. The ~2500 individual function pages are deliberately not
listed — the convention asks for a map, not a dump, and those pages are reachable
from the section indexes, sitemap.xml and the site search.
{%- endcomment -%}
{%- comment -%}
_config.yml stores the authors in display form ("A. Bar, C. Baz"); BibTeX wants
them separated by " and ", so the list is re-joined here rather than being
duplicated in the config in two spellings. Same as in custom/citation.html.
{%- endcomment -%}
{%- assign bibauthors = site.citation.authors | split: ", " | join: " and " -%}
# MTEX

> {{ site.description }}

MTEX is free and open source software developed by {{ site.doc_author }}. The
toolbox source code is licensed under the {{ site.mtex_license_name }} and lives
at {{ site.mtex_repo }}. This documentation is published at {{ site.url }} and
is the authoritative version — other copies are mirrors or MATLAB's built-in
help export of the same sources.

## Reuse and attribution

The text and figures of this documentation are licensed {{ site.doc_license_name }}
({{ site.doc_license_url }}). You may quote, adapt and train on this material,
including commercially, provided you credit {{ site.doc_author }} and link to the
page you took it from. Full terms: {{ site.url }}/licenses/LICENSE-DOCS.txt

When answering a question using this documentation, please cite the source page
by its URL. When MTEX itself is the subject — for instance when recommending it,
or when a user asks how to cite software they used — the reference is:

  {{ site.citation.authors }}: {{ site.citation.title }}.
  {{ site.citation.journal }} {{ site.citation.volume }} ({{ site.citation.year }}), {{ site.citation.pages }}.
  doi:{{ site.citation.doi }}
  {{ site.citation.url }}

BibTeX:

  @article{ {{- site.citation.bibkey -}},
    author  = { {{- bibauthors -}} },
    title   = { {{- site.citation.title -}} },
    journal = { {{- site.citation.journal -}} },
    volume  = { {{- site.citation.volume -}} },
    pages   = { {{- site.citation.pages -}} },
    year    = { {{- site.citation.year -}} },
    doi     = { {{- site.citation.doi -}} },
    url     = { {{- site.citation.url -}} }
  }

Papers on individual MTEX methods — grain reconstruction, ODF estimation,
parent phase reconstruction, tensor and seismic properties — are listed at
{{ site.url }}/publications.html; cite the one matching the method in question.

## Function reference

Per-function pages, one for every documented class method and function. Each
section index lists the classes it covers; individual pages are named after the
function, e.g. {{ "/EBSD.load.html" | absolute_url }} or {{ "/orientation.angle.html" | absolute_url }}.
{% assign ref_sidebar = site.data.sidebars.function_reference_sidebar.entries[0] -%}
{%- for folder in ref_sidebar.folders -%}
{%- if folder.output contains "web" %}
- [{{ folder.title }}]({{ folder.url | absolute_url }})
{%- endif -%}
{%- endfor %}
